arxiv-1502-03507.title: Sc 20 C 60 : A Volleyballene
arxiv-1502-03507.creator: Jing Wang 1,2, Hong-Man Ma 1, Ying Liu 1,3
arxiv-1502-03507.description: Abstract An exceptionally stable hollow cage containing 20 scandiums and 60 carbons was identified. This Sc 20 C 60 molecular cluster has a T h T_{h} point group symmetry and a volleyball-like shape, that we refer to below as ”Volleyballene”.

arxiv-2110-14921.title: 3D Object Tracking with Transformer
arxiv-2110-14921.creator: Yubo Cui 1,, Zheng Fang, Jiayao Shan, Zuoxu Gu, Sifan Zhou
arxiv-2110-14921.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Yubo Cui 1,, Zheng Fang, Jiayao Shan, Zuoxu Gu, Sifan Zhou. Feature fusion and similarity computation are two core problems in 3D object tracking, especially for object tracking using sparse and disordered point clouds. Feature fusion could make similarity computing more efficient by including target object information. However, most existing LiDAR-based approaches directly use the extracted point cloud feature to compute similarity while ignoring the attention changes of object regions during tracking.

arxiv-2209-06259.title: Designing Biological Sequences via Meta-Reinforcement Learning and Bayesian Optimization
arxiv-2209-06259.creator: Leo FengPadideh NouriAneri Muni, Yoshua Bengio, Pierre-Luc Bacon Mila – Université de Montréal
arxiv-2209-06259.description: Abstract The ability to accelerate the design of biological sequences can have a substantial impact on the progress of the medical field. The problem can be framed as a global optimization problem where the objective is an expensive black-box function such that we can query large batches restricted with a limitation of a low number of rounds.

arxiv-2211-02300.title: Elimination of Non-Novel Segments at Multi-Scale for Few-Shot Segmentation
arxiv-2211-02300.creator: Alper Kayabaşı, Gülin Tüfekci, İlkay Ulusoy
arxiv-2211-02300.description: Abstract Few-shot segmentation aims to devise a generalizing model that segments query images from unseen classes during training with the guidance of a few support images whose class tally with the class of the query. There exist two domain-specific problems mentioned in the previous works, namely spatial inconsistency and bias towards seen classes.

arxiv-2304-12135.title: Strongly Reduced Lattice Bases
arxiv-2304-12135.creator: Christian Porter
arxiv-2304-12135.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Christian Porter. In this paper, we show that for each lattice basis, there exists an equivalent basis which we describe as “strongly reduced”. We show that bases reduced in this manner exhibit rather “short” basis vectors, that is, the length of the i i th basis vector of a strongly reduced basis is upper bounded by a polynomial factor in i i multiplied by the i i th successive minima of the lattice.

arxiv-2401-01797.title: Parabolic Anderson model in bounded domains of recurrent metric measure spaces
arxiv-2401-01797.creator: F. Baudoin, L. Chen, C.H. Huang, C. Ouyang, S. Tindel, J. Wang
arxiv-2401-01797.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by F. Baudoin, L. Chen, C.H. Huang, C. Ouyang, S. Tindel, J. Wang. A metric measure space equipped with a Dirichlet form is called recurrent if its Hausdorff dimension is less than its walk dimension.

arxiv-2502-01100.title: ZebraLogic: On the Scaling Limits of LLMs for Logical Reasoning
arxiv-2502-01100.creator: Bill Yuchen Lin, Ronan Le Bras, Kyle Richardson, Ashish Sabharwal, Radha Poovendran, Peter Clark, Yejin Choi
arxiv-2502-01100.description: Abstract We investigate the logical reasoning capabilities of large language models (LLMs) and their scalability in complex non-monotonic reasoning. To this end, we introduce ZebraLogic, a comprehensive evaluation framework for assessing LLM reasoning performance on logic grid puzzles derived from constraint satisfaction problems (CSPs).

arxiv-2502-12153.title: Gravitational waves from the Axiverse
arxiv-2502-12153.creator: Saurav Das, Francesc Ferrer
arxiv-2502-12153.description: Abstract Models with axion like particles (ALPs) often predict the formation of a string-domain wall network in the early universe. We study how such networks of defects appear in the context of string theory, and discuss the conditions for their long-term stability.

arxiv-2506-20152.title: Loss-Aware Automatic Selection of Structured Pruning Criteria for Deep Neural Network Acceleration Journal: Elsevier Image and Vision Computing Journal
arxiv-2506-20152.creator: Deepak Ghimire, Kilho Lee, Seong-heum Kim
arxiv-2506-20152.description: Abstract Structured pruning is a well-established technique for compressing neural networks, making it suitable for deployment in resource-limited edge devices. This paper presents an efficient Loss-Aware Automatic Selection of Structured Pruning Criteria (LAASP) for slimming and accelerating deep neural networks.

arxiv-2509-17540.creator: Jun-Feng Wang 1,2, De-Shun Zhang 1,2, Zhi-Feng Sun 1,2,3,4

britannica-1911-wellington-arthur-welles.creator: Encyclopaedia Britannica
britannica-1911-wellington-arthur-welles.description: Article 'Wellington, Arthur Wellesley, 1st Duke of' from the 1911 Encyclopædia Britannica (Volume 28), the classic English-language general encyclopedia, now in the public domain. to the estates of Garrett Wesley, a distant relative of the famous divine. In Wellington’s early letters the family name is spelt Wesley; the change to Wellesley seems to have been made about 1790. Arthur (born in Ireland in 1769 ) was sent to Eton, and subsequently to a military college at Angers.

plos-pone-0356528.description: IoT based automated early detection and real time environmental monitoring for poultry farming in developing countries

pmc-11439080.title: Oral microbial diversity in 18th century African individuals from South Carolina
pmc-11439080.creator: Raquel E. Fleskes, Sarah J. Johnson, Tanvi P. Honap, Christopher A. Abin, Joanna K. Gilmore, La’Sheia Oubré, Wolf D. Bueschgen, Suzanne M. Abel, Ade A. Ofunniyin, Cecil M. Lewis, Theodore G. Schurr
pmc-11439080.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). As part of the Anson Street African Burial Ground Project, we characterized the oral microbiomes of twelve 18th century African-descended individuals (Ancestors) from Charleston, South Carolina, USA, to study their oral health and diet. We found that their oral microbiome composition resembled that of other historic (18th-19th century) dental calculus samples but differed from that of modern samples, and was not influenced by indicators of oral health and wear observed in the dentition.

pmc-11680150.title: Determination and Prediction of Available Energy in 13 Cereal Feed Ingredients for Growing Pigs
pmc-11680150.creator: Jinbiao Zhao, Xiaoming Song, Meiyu Yang, Ge Zhang, Ling Liu
pmc-11680150.description: Simple SummaryIt could be useful to rapidly and accurately evaluate the available energy in feed ingredients when formulating pig feed. Some researchers have studied equations for predicting the available energy for pigs using the chemical composition of a single cereal sample. Currently, many mixed feed ingredients are used to prepare pig feed.

pmc-12421600.title: Design of aSpiration based thrombectomy in acUte large vessel oCclusive sTroke with dIfferent etiOlogies: a real-world multiceNtre (SUCTION) study
pmc-12421600.creator: Peng Yan, Maoyu Li, Lei Yang, Cunfeng Song, Shudong Liu, Xiaohui Chen, Shengli Chen, Haicheng Yuan, Kai Li, Qiang Guo, Hui Liu, Yunnan Lu, Feng Wang, Lei Mu, Zequn Li, Jianfeng Han, Yong Sun, Hao Qin, Liqun Jiao, QinJian Sun, SUCTION study Investigators
pmc-12421600.description: IntroductionIntracranial atherosclerosis is the main cause of stroke globally, with acute large vessel occlusive (LVO) stroke being a predominant contributor to stroke-related mortality. In recent years, aspiration thrombectomy (AT) has emerged as a novel therapeutic method for treating acute LVO stroke.

pmc-12442117.title: Sustainability of hand hygiene compliance in a crowded emergency and trauma setting within a public tertiary healthcare facility
pmc-12442117.creator: Peh Yee Lee, Jiancong Wang, Siti Nur Zulydiana Binti Abang Ahmad, Alicia Ak Juan, Yew Fong Lee
pmc-12442117.description: Introduction: Crowded Emergency and Trauma Department (ETD) have been associated with adverse patient outcomes and higher mortality rates. Crowding and lack of alcohol-based hand rubs (ABHRs) have been found to correlate with lower compliance to hand hygiene (HH) protocols among healthcare workers (HWs).

pmc-12919381.title: Antimicrobial functional ingredients used in hand hygiene products: a cross-sectional survey on regional e-commerce platforms in Wuhan area of China
pmc-12919381.creator: Xintong Chen, Jun Wang
pmc-12919381.description: BackgroundHand hygiene products containing antimicrobial functional ingredients have become daily products for many people during the post-pandemic period. However, their current market scenarios have not been well explored.ObjectiveTo provide an overview of antimicrobial functional ingredients in hand sanitizer products marketed to the public in Wuhan, China.MethodsThis cross-sectional product survey was conducted in September 2023.

pmc-13183606.title: Reconstructing cerebral lymphatic clearance: an emerging target in the Alzheimer's disease therapeutic pipeline
pmc-13183606.creator: Jiheng Zhang, Jiren Zhang, Jian Ding, Xian Zhang, Yuhua Wang, Wei Wei, Yan Chai, Shu Zhang, Xin Chen
pmc-13183606.description: Neurotoxic protein accumulation is widely recognized as a key feature of Alzheimer's disease (AD), and increasing evidence indicates that impaired brain clearance associated with dysfunction of the meningeal lymphatic and glymphatic may contribute to this process. Disruption of these pathways may weaken homeostatic mechanisms and facilitate amyloid‑β and tau buildup.

pmc-13276786.title: 3D‐Printed Platforms for Enzyme Immobilisation Screening and Direct Translation into Continuous‐Flow Biocatalysis
pmc-13276786.creator: Simone Marchetti, Gianluca Palmara, Cristopher Tinajero, Luis David Lisintuña, Paulo Roberto de Oliveira, Marcileia Zanatta, Victor Sans
pmc-13276786.description: The development of immobilised biocatalysts for continuous‐flow processes is still largely based on laborious trial‐and‐error screening, and conditions optimised on conventional carriers are often not directly transferable to structured reactors. Here, we introduce a 3D‐printed methodology that integrates high‐throughput screening of enzyme immobilisation with implementation in a continuous‐flow reactor using the same photopolymeric formulation.

pmc-13432021.title: Lymph node stromal topology as a hidden regulator of breast cancer outcome: commentary on reticular network analysis†
pmc-13432021.creator: Andrea Vethencourt, Roberto Salgado, Eva Gonzalez‐Suarez
pmc-13432021.description: The axillary lymph node remains a cornerstone of breast cancer staging and therapeutic decision‐making, yet it is still largely interpreted through a static anatomical framework. Emerging evidence challenges this paradigm, positioning tumor‐draining lymph nodes as dynamic immunological ecosystems that actively regulate tumor progression and host response.

pmc-13475086.title: Targeting GRP75 by natural compound polyphyllin II triggers mitochondrial calcium overload and pyroptosis to potentiate cancer immunotherapy
pmc-13475086.creator: Yuting Wang, Jingwen Dong, Yu Long, Liping Li, Cuicui Sun, Ruoqi Li, Jiayu Zhang, Yichen Liu, Zipeng Yao, Shuqi Wang, Ke Li, Mingxiao Yin, Xinbo Zhou, Na Zhang, Hongbin Deng
pmc-13475086.description: BackgroundImmune checkpoint blockade (ICB) therapy has emerged as a pivotal cancer treatment by activating antitumor immunity. However, its clinical efficacy remains limited in many patients, highlighting the need for combination strategies to overcome resistance. Inducing immunogenic cell death (ICD) represents a promising approach to remodel the immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment and improve ICB efficacy.

pmc-13546638.title: A Physiologically-Based Pharmacokinetic Model to Predict Posaconazole Suspension Exposure and Optimize Dosing Strategy in Pediatric Hematology Patients: Incorporating the Impact of Food Intake
pmc-13546638.creator: Juan Wu, Xia Qin, Xiaohang Huang, Dengyu Wang, Cheng Jin, Shiying Huang, Zhuo Li, Manman Liu
pmc-13546638.description: ObjectiveThis study aimed to develop and validate a physiologically based pharmacokinetic (PBPK) model for posaconazole oral suspension in pediatric hematology patients to predict systemic exposure and optimize dose regimens that incorporate food intake.MethodsA PBPK model was established and validated in adults. The model was then extrapolated to pediatric patients by integrating age-specific physiological parameters.

pmc-13615600.title: The burden of suicide by paraquat poisoning in Taiwan (1987–2017): trends, geographic variations, and demographic characteristics
pmc-13615600.creator: Hwei Yuen Chang, Chao-Ying Tu, Chien-Yu Lin, Chia-Yueh Hsu, Tzung-Hai Yen, David Gunnell, Michael Eddleston, Shu-Sen Chang
pmc-13615600.description: BackgroundPesticide self-poisoning accounts for 14%–20% of global suicides. Paraquat, a highly lethal pesticide, is involved in a considerable number of suicides in some countries. This study investigated the burden, trends, geographic variations, and demographic characteristics of pesticide and paraquat suicides in Taiwan.MethodsSuicide data (1987, 1992, 1997, and 2002–2017) were obtained from Taiwan’s cause-of-death mortality data files.

uslaw-usc-t22-s5702.title: 22 U.S.C. § 5702 — Definitions
uslaw-usc-t22-s5702.creator: United States Congress
uslaw-usc-t22-s5702.description: United States Code, Title 22 (Foreign Relations And Intercourse); Chapter 66 (United States-Hong Kong Policy). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. For purposes of this chapter— (1) the term “Hong Kong” means, prior to July 1, 1997, the British Dependent Territory of Hong Kong, and on and after July 1, 1997, the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region of the People’s Republic of China.
